jobs.title: Environmental Scientist-Inspector
jobs.description:
Job Description And Duties

Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking an Environmental Scientist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electrical Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.

Under general direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist Supervisor of the Inspections & Investigations Branch the incumbent will develop inspection plans to assess electrical corporation performance with approved Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMPs), conduct inspections of vegetation near electrical infrastructure, write and review inspection reports, and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, and the environment. Incumbent will also conduct investigations into concerns raised by external parties regarding potential WMP findings, conduct critical and/or sensitive scientific investigations and studies and prepare guidance, policy, planning, or regulatory documents on issues of importance to the department as assigned. Incumbent will identify issues found in the field and elevate to the Supervisor with proposed recommendations. The incumbent will develop and maintain positive relationships with internal and external agency partners. The incumbent will be a subject matter expert on vegetation management inspection programs to assess electrical utility performance with approved WMPs and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, climate change and the environment.

The reporting location for this position is California Natural Resources Agency Building located at 715 P Street, Sacramento, CA 95814.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Desirable Qualifications

In addition to evaluating each candidate's relative ability, as demonstrated by quality and breadth of experience, the following factors will provide the basis for competitively evaluating each candidate:

Knowledge of wildfire, vegetation management and/or forestry science and approaches to reducing wildfire risk.
Experience performing inspections, documenting and communicating findings.
Experience as a technical scientist working with members of the public, external stakeholders, and agency representatives
Ability to effectively communicate and present complex scientific findings to non-scientific audiences through written reports and presentations.
Ability to coordinate with individuals from different professional backgrounds.
Experience with regulatory processes and compliance and enforcement of regulations.
Experience working under tight timelines.

jobs.description:
About Exponent

Exponent
is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Our vision is to engage multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drives our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career through mentoring, sponsorship, and a culture of learning. Thanks for your interest in joining our team!  

Key statistics:

950+ Consultants
640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Geologist
for our Civil & Structural Engineering
Practice in Los Angeles, CA
or Oakland, CA
. In this role , you will work as part of a team responsible for providing professional services in the areas of engineering geology, remote sensing, GIS, mapping, and geophysics for a range of projects involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards. This position will provide technically challenging work with excellent opportunities to grow within the firm.

You will be responsible for

Conducting field inspections and subsurface explorations (to determine causes of failure of geotechnical systems e.g. slopes, foundations, tunnels, levees, and dams).
Evaluating and characterizing site conditions (for root cause of failure analyses and conceptual mitigation design)
Creation of Geospatial models including GIS and subsurface models
Creation of topographic maps and thematic maps
Assisting with peer review of geologic and geotechnical engineering documents

You Will Have The Following Skills And Qualifications

Ph.D. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology or a related field from an accredited university
Alternatively, a M.S. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology , or a related field , from an accredited university plus 5 years of experience
Ability to become a licensed professional Geologist (PG) or Geophysicist (PGP) in at least one state within three years
Experience , or related coursework in , Geotechnical Engineering, and Groundwater/Surface Water Hydrology are a strong plus
Demonstrated excellence in coursework and/or fieldwork involving geologic characterization and mapping; experience with geotechnical subsurface investigation techniques a strong plus
Experience with GIS modeling software, graphic software, and imaging software
Ability to gather information from a wide variety of sources (e.g., field investigations, document reviews, and interviews) and to synthetize and convey technical conclusions to individuals in engineering, business, and industry
Strong analytical, field investigation, and critical thinking skills
Attention to detail, dedication to quality and accuracy, desire to work in a fast-paced environment, and effective leadership skills
Strong publication record in peer - reviewed journals or conference proceedings or demonstrated leadership or activity in geologic professional societies, boards, or commissions
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Strong interest in a career primarily involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards

Local Language is a hybrid art consulting and fabrication studio that curates and creates art collections that tell the unique story of each project. From concept to installation, Local Language produces sculptural designs, curated collections, and architectural installations for commercial properties nationwide. The studio manages the full process from ideation and bespoke art fabrication to project management and installation.

The Project Coordinator is a full-time, on-site role in Oakland, CA.
This role supports the planning and execution of projects, coordinating production approvals, and communication between internal teams, external vendors, and clients.

Day-to-day responsibilities include tracking project milestones, coordinating design sample approvals, maintaining project documentation, and coordinating logistics. The Project Coordinator assists with sourcing materials, pushing orders into production, and ensuring that quality standards and client requirements are met. This role also contributes to problem-solving on active projects and helps maintain efficient studio operations.

Project coordination and organizational skills, including scheduling, timeline management, and task tracking.
Experience with client communication, stakeholder coordination, and clear, professional correspondence.
Familiarity with art fabrication, design, or creative production processes, ideally within an art, architecture, or fabrication studio environment.

Comfort working in a hands-on, fast paced studio environment
Ability to collaborate in a diverse, creative team environment and adapt to evolving project needs.
Relevant education or experience in art, design, project management, or a related field

jobs.title: SAP S/4HANA Project Coordinator/Project manager
jobs.description:
Job Title: SAP S/4HANA Project Coordinator/Project manager

Location: Milpitas, CA 95035 (Onsite)
Duration: 12+ Months

Job Details:

Minimum years of experience required: Minimum 10 years of professional IT or Business Transformation experience with 3+ years in PMO, project coordination, testing, change management, procurement, or ERP program support

Must Have Skills:

PMO/Project Coordination, SAP S/4HANA or ERP transformation support, Testing (SIT/UAT), Change Management, Business Readiness, Documentation Review, Defect Tracking, Stakeholder Coordination, JIRA, SharePoint, MS Teams, Excel, PowerPoint.

Nice to Have Skills:

SAP Ariba, SAP ECC, Source-to-Pay (S2P)/Procure-to-Pay (P2P) process knowledge, Training Coordination, Cutover & Go-Live Support, Global stakeholder management, APAC time-zone support experience.

Detailed Job Description:

Role Purpose:

Provide project coordination and execution support for Project ATLAS across the remaining S/4HANA build, testing, change management, business readiness, and go-live activities. The contingent worker will work under the direction of the S2P Business Leader and designated workstream owners. The role is responsible for documentation review, coordination, tracking, testing execution, and follow-up. Final decisions, solution ownership, design approval, and business or system recommendations remain with SanDisk business owners, IT, and authorized program leadership.

Role Boundaries:

Operate as a support and execution resource, not as the business process owner, solution owner, or final decision maker.
Do not independently approve designs, requirements, scope changes, test sign-off, readiness decisions, or go-live decisions.
Do not independently propose or select business or technical solutions; document options and inputs provided by accountable owners.
Escalate unresolved issues, risks, conflicts, and decision requirements to the appropriate SanDisk owner.
Perform activities based on approved plans, processes, requirements, test scripts, and direction from accountable workstream owners.

Key Organizational Relationships

S2P Business Leader and workstream owners
Business SMEs and regional stakeholders
IT, testing, and data teams
System Integrator Deloitte
Change management, training, communications, and cutover teams

Key Responsibilities

1. Build Phase Support:

Support the remaining S/4HANA and Ariba build activities through coordination, documentation, status tracking, and follow-up.
Review project documentation for completeness, consistency, traceability, and alignment with approved inputs; consolidate comments for owner review.
Capture meeting notes, feedback, actions, risks, assumptions, decisions, dependencies, and due dates.
Track configuration, RICEFW, functional specification, data, and dependency status based on updates from responsible owners.
Coordinate follow-up among business SMEs, IT, and Deloitte and escalate overdue or unresolved items to the designated owner.
Prepare consolidated status information and supporting materials for review by the S2P Business Leader or workstream owner.

2. Testing Support and Execution:

Support SIT and UAT preparation using approved test scope, scenarios, test cases, data requirements, tester assignments, and schedules.
Review test cases and evidence for completeness and traceability to approved requirements and processes; route gaps to the responsible owner.
Perform assigned testing activities using approved test scripts and document actual results and supporting evidence.
Maintain testing trackers covering readiness, coverage, execution progress, defects, retesting, evidence, and sign-off inputs.
Coordinate tester communications, working sessions, access needs, data needs, and follow-up actions.
Consolidate testing results and evidence for review and approval by authorized business and IT owners.

3. Change Management and Business Readiness Support:

Support execution of the approved change management and business readiness plans.
Coordinate stakeholder lists, change-impact reviews, readiness activities, and follow-up across impacted functions, roles, and regions.
Review change-impact, process, training, and communication documents for completeness, consistency, and traceability; consolidate feedback for owner approval.
Maintain traceability among approved future-state processes, system changes, impacted roles, training content, communications, and readiness actions.
Coordinate training logistics, including audience lists, material review cycles, SME feedback, scheduling, attendance, completion tracking, and feedback collection.
Support communication execution by coordinating draft reviews, audience validation, approvals, scheduling, and distribution tracking.
Track stakeholder engagement, adoption concerns, resistance themes, readiness gaps, mitigation actions, owners, and due dates.
Prepare readiness trackers, dashboards, and status summaries for review by change management and business owners.

4. Go-Live and Stabilization Support:

Track approved readiness criteria, cutover activities, business dependencies, open items, and required evidence.
Coordinate cutover, communication, training, hyper care, and support-transition activities under the direction of accountable owners.
Maintain issue, action, and adoption-feedback trackers during go-live and stabilization.
Consolidate status, lessons learned, and outstanding actions for owner review and closure.

5. Project Coordination and Reporting:

Maintain integrated schedules and trackers covering build, testing, change management, training, communications, and business readiness.
Prepare draft weekly status updates, risk summaries, meeting materials, and escalation packs for owner review.
Facilitate working sessions, document minutes and actions, and follow up with assigned owners.
Provide accurate and timely documentation without representing support inputs as final decisions or approvals.
Other tasks assigned by the Manager.

Core Skills & Experience:

Experience providing PMO, project coordination, testing, or change management support in ERP or business transformation programs.
Exposure to SAP S/4HANA, Ariba, ECC, or similar enterprise platforms is preferred.
Working knowledge of Source-to-Pay or Procure-to-Pay processes.
Hands-on experience with documentation review, test execution, defect tracking, training coordination, and readiness tracking.
Strong organization, documentation, communication, meeting facilitation, and stakeholder follow-up skills.
Ability to work within defined governance, follow approved direction, and escalate matters requiring owner decisions.
Familiarity with JIRA, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, or similar collaboration and tracking tools.

Preferred Profile:

3+ years of project coordination, PMO, testing, change management, procurement, or ERP program support experience.
Minimum 10 years of professional IT or Business Transformation experience.
Be able to adapt to flexible workshops to support APAC time zones whenever required.
Experience working with business SMEs, IT teams, and system integrator partners in a global environment.
Comfortable performing detailed execution and follow-up across multiple workstreams and time zones.
Be able to adapt to flexible workshops to support APAC time zones.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Company Description
Advanced Mobility Group (AMG) is a consulting firm focused on reshaping transportation through smart, sustainable mobility solutions. 511 CCTA, Street Smarts Contra Costa (SSCC), and Walk N Roll (WNR) are programs of the Contra Costa Transportation Authority, managed by Advanced Mobility Group. 511 CCTA provides programs, incentives, and resources to encourage the use of alternative (non-drive alone) modes of transportation for commute and local trips in Contra Costa County. SSCC provides traffic safety education and active transportation (biking/walking) encouragement programs for all public elementary and middle schools located in central, eastern, and Lamorinda areas of Contra Costa County. WNR is an active transportation program that encourages students to walk or bike to school every week.

Role Description
The Program Coordinator will deliver engaging stage performances in elementary school assemblies. Script memorization is required, and prior acting experience is highly desired. The middle school program requires the coordinator to engage with students one-on-one and in group settings to encourage safe active transportation during interactive Walk/Bike to School events. The coordinator will assist at occasional after-school or evening bicycle rodeos, PTA meetings and presentations. Other tasks include packing materials and handling event preparation, making various deliveries, and occasionally working at in-person community and school events on evenings/weekends. The coordinator will also provide customer service for various 511 CCTA commuter programs, facilitate mailings, and participate in employer events. The coordinator must be physically able to lift large and heavy equipment, have a valid driver’s license, and a clean driving record. Punctuality is critical for this position.

Essential Duties:

Street Smarts Contra Costa (SSCC) Tasks:

·        Elementary school assemblies: Street Smarts provides safety education to all K-5 students by performing engaging school assemblies for grades K-2 and 3-5. Memorization of two 30-minute scripts and rehearsals with a co-Coordinator are required. Operation of a robotic car during assemblies is also required (training provided). Performer must be able to use a microphone and manipulate slideshows via remote control, iPad, and/or laptop. Additional tasks: packing materials, loading, and unloading the company van and school stages of large props and AV equipment, travel (paid time) between the Walnut Creek office and schools, interaction with school staff, and other related miscellaneous tasks. Assemblies take place during the school day; the workday for these events typically starts between 6:00-7:30am. A typical school year includes approximately 30-50 assembly days.

·        Middle school Blender Bike events: Street Smarts encourages middle school students to use active transportation to school by hosting fun Walk & Roll to School Day events featuring two stationary blender bikes that are used to make lemonade slushies. Tasks include packing equipment and materials, loading and unloading the company van, travel (paid time) between the Walnut Creek office and schools, interaction and education with students, helmet fittings, cleaning of equipment after event, and other related miscellaneous tasks. Blender events take place for one hour before the first bell; the workday for these events typically starts before 7am. A typical school year includes approximately 10-15 blender bike events.

·        International Walk/Bike to School Day events (typically held in October and May): prepare and deliver event materials to participating schools, using the company vehicle.

Walk N Roll (WNR) Tasks:

·        Attending launch days for the Walk N Roll program to assist new schools with welcoming, organizing, and scanning students. These events typically start between 7:00-7:30am.

·        Assisting with occasional after school and/or evening bicycle
rodeos.
·        Giving presentations at schools and other stakeholder events, meetings with parent volunteers and/or school personnel.
·        Training and leading volunteers.
·        Other tasks may include sorting, packing, creating, and delivering necessary supplies to schools, travel between the Walnut Creek office and participating schools, and other related miscellaneous tasks.

511 CCTA Tasks:
·        Community events: pack materials, coordinate with organizations, interact with members of the public, be able to provide accurate information about all programs and resources
·        Summer Bike and Winter Walk Challenges: perform customer service via email
·        Crosstrain on all 511 CCTA programs and program support tasks, including but not limited to the E-Bike Rebate, Big Win, invoicing, and other programs
·        Giving presentations to various stakeholders as needed
·        Make miscellaneous deliveries and purchases of supplies.

Knowledge, Skills, and Special Abilities Required:

·        Acting / performing / public speaking expertise

·        Script memorization

·        Proficient English speaker; Spanish and/or Dari fluency desired

·        Ability and willingness to learn how to operate a remote-controlled robotic car - while voice acting a script from off stage

·        Ability to communicate effectively with children, co-workers, school officials, and the public

·        Ability to lift 50 pounds

·        Knowledge of/or ability to learn how to operate a slideshow presentation using a projector, iPad, laptop, microphone, and speaker system

·        Ability to be punctual and reliable

·        Highly sought character traits: leadership, creativity, enthusiasm, sense of humor, and ability to solve problems.

Experience and Education:

·        Acting experience preferred

·        Two years’ experience working or volunteering in an educational setting, performing, in-person community outreach, acting, and/or working in a youth recreational setting such as a summer camp or youth sports

·        Experience with presentations, training others, and Microsoft Office Suite preferred

·        A college degree is preferred; or

·        An equivalent combination of experience and education sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job such as those listed above.

Other requirements:

Valid CA driver’s license and a clean driving record.

The role is primarily office-based, with regular attendance at schools and community events as part of program delivery, outreach, and community engagement.

Fingerprinting and background check for eligibility to perform in public schools.

Salary: $30-$40 per hour with benefits, depending on experience and education

Interested candidates, please send resumes to Cara De Jong cara@amobility.com

jobs.title: REC ‘N THE STREETS Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Description

Seattle Parks and Recreation (SPR) is a national leader and innovator in the services and programs we provide to our residents who enjoy our public spaces such as parks, community centers, specialty gardens and swimming pools. Our mission is to equip employees and the public for well-being as we support healthy people, a thriving environment and vibrant community. We provide safe and accessible spaces for residents and visitors to work, recreate, rejuvenate and enhance quality of life and wellness for children, teenagers, adults and seniors. Delivering excellent customer service to all is a core value.

Equity & Inclusion:
Seattle Parks and Recreation commits to advancing equity and social justice in our department and in every neighborhood by growing a dynamic and diverse workforce, developing strong investments, growth opportunities and beneficial partner strategies as we acknowledge and pledge to close disparities created by historical practices which often hindered workforce development, environmental justice, access to quality open spaces, programs and facilities.

The Recreation and Aquatics Division
eliminates barriers through responsive, exceptional recreation services. We operate over 50 recreation facilities (community centers, teen centers, pools, school-based learning centers, environmental learning centers, and boating and sailing centers) and provide opportunities for people to play, learn, and lead healthy, active lives. Our programs and events include fitness and athletics, licensed childcare and preschool, swimming and boating, youth development and job preparation, academic enrichment, and more -- including programs designed for older adults and people with disabilities, as well as grant and partnership programs designed and implemented with immigrant and refugee communities. With nearly 300 regular employees and a budget of nearly $40 million annually, Recreation is a major operation with significant impact on the communities we serve. In addition to our current operations, we also strive to constantly improve the ways we serve Seattle’s residents, specifically through implementation of the SPR Strategic Plan, innovation in our facility staffing and programming approaches, and learning from national best practices and quality standards.

This position coordinates and leads the Rec ‘N The Streets (RNTS) program of the Seattle Parks and Recreation Outdoor Activation Mobile Recreation Office, under the general supervision of the Senior Recreation Program Coordinator. The Rec ‘N The Streets Program Coordinator plans, organizes, and coordinates the development and implementation of recreation activities into programs and facilities within various districts (approximately 40 locations). This position assists/guides staff in developing programming ideas and implementation plans; and supervises the activities of program staff, contractors, volunteers, and occasionally youth employees.

The Rec ‘N The Streets Coordinator meets with internal and external stakeholders, community members and community-based organizations to develop and implement programs that meet the expressed needs of diverse, and/or traditionally underserved populations in various communities within the City of Seattle. This position provides technical expertise to the recreation division for city-wide programs. This position is expected to meet time sensitive deadlines, monitor and track budget expenses, equipment acquisition, vehicle repair and maintenance associated with the Rec ‘N the Streets program.

Job Responsibilities

Manage the daily operational logistics, planning, and implementation of the RNTS program. This includes on-site training and monitoring staff performance.
Supervise 12 permanent Recreation Leaders in off-peak season and up to 10 additional temporary Recreation Leaders during peak season. Oversee the organization of special events managing the staffing and equipment schedule.
Coordinate and evaluate RNTS Programs for compliance with the Commission for Accreditation of Park and Recreation Agencies programming standards (CAPRA). Set goals and guidelines that incorporate adult and youth program quality, recreation success domains, targets, outcomes and Compliance with City Policy.
Develop both internal and external reports utilizing outcome frameworks, compiling and analyzing data from participant satisfaction surveys and feedback forms, that informs new programming and modify existing programs.
Participate in preparation of training and professional development of Jr Team members.
Meet with Neighborhood and Community groups to develop contracts and partnerships with mutually advantages’ goals.
Responsible for maintaining program revenue goals, administering, and monitoring RNTS budget while maintaining inventory control.
Recruit, train, and evaluate subordinate staff; and recommend selection of staff.
Develop policies and procedures for RNTS activations.
Respond to comments, questions, and complaints from program participants.
Perform other related duties of a comparable level/type as assigned.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Summary Statement

Turn GIS and data into better decisions, smarter workflows, and stronger emergency response.

The Boise Fire Department is seeking a GIS Data Analyst to help transform operational and dispatch data into actionable insights that improve how the department works and serves the community. This mid-level role will leverage the Esri platform, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Field Maps, and ArcGIS Survey123 Connect, to develop, maintain, analyze, and improve GIS-based data and workflows across the department.

Working closely with personnel throughout the organization and supporting command staff, this position will analyze dispatch and operational data, identify trends and opportunities, improve business processes, and develop innovative GIS and data solutions. The GIS Data Analyst will look for ways to automate repetitive tasks, streamline workflows, improve data quality and accessibility, and build sustainable solutions that increase efficiency over time.

This is an opportunity for a GIS professional who wants to go beyond mapping—to solve operational problems, connect people and data, automate processes, and help leadership make informed, strategic decisions. The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on Esri experience, analytical thinking, curiosity, and a proactive approach to finding ways technology and data can make the Boise Fire Department more effective.

To ensure internal equity and alignment with the approved budget for this position, offers are made within the posted hiring range. Although the hiring range is fixed, employees receive an exceptional benefits and total rewards package that enhances the overall value of employment with the City of Boise.

Required Knowledge, Experience, And Training

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, economics, mathematics, business administration or a related field
Three years of experience performing highly complex business analysis, data science or analytics
An equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

Special Requirements

Applicants must be able to pass:

City of Boise background check processes which includes a criminal history check and reference checks in accordance with the City of Boise Hiring Process Regulation
Boise Police Department Criminal Justice Information System Background Check (BPD CJIS)
Hybrid Work Eligible

Why the City of Boise?

The benefits are real and among the best in the Treasure Valley:

Zero-cost premium medical coverage for you and your family (an estimated $10,000 - 20,000 value)
PERSI retirement (11.96% Employer Contribution) plus employer-matched 401(k)/457b

Tuition reimbursement and free local bus pass

Essential Functions

Develops digital maps through a geographic information system (GIS). Integrates base maps, data layers, tabular data and other GIS analysis with records management and other software systems. Builds mapping applications and dashboards. Mines, extracts and analyzes data to support strategic projects. Reviews and evaluates current workflow processes. Acquires and maintains new datasets and corresponding metadata, including usage of the city data warehouse.

Initiates and develops business analyses, data sets and dashboards for review. Researches and analyzes trends, practices, laws and statistics to develop options and recommendations. Identifies and measures business operations updates to evaluate performance. Identifies, develops and/or recommends outcome-based measures, forecasts, scenarios and efficiencies. Creates maps, reports, dashboards and presentations to communicate data and analysis.

Utilizes various databases to integrate statistical data for fiscal research, resources/staffing or asset impact, performance measures and indicators and other analyses. Monitors data sets for quality control and coordinates consistency within and across data sets. Troubleshoots and resolves data matters. Defines data standards in coordination with internal and external agency partners. Participates and collaborates in data communities.

Develops strong partnerships and learns all aspects of the business for a positive impact. Designs, plans and maintains the service deployment model. Performs resource deployment analysis. Refines data into risk categories and develops risk demand zones. Identifies and analyzes data sets to model risk and prepares deliverables. Supports emergency planning, emergency management and major disaster response events as well as the Incident Management Team (IMT).

Prepares, analyzes and interprets data for critical department and city reports. Analyzes historical call volume data to look for trends and project future department needs. Creates custom and auto-generated reports, including data from area-specific system technology, for data analysis and commonly used and/or new metrics within the department through engaging data visualization and presentation. Delivers applicable training to department personnel and assists with team coordination.

Performs other duties as assigned. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this position at any time.

Area-specific system technology.

jobs.title: GIS Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Description

Position Overview:

The Harris County Fire Marshal's Office (HCFMO) is seeking a skilled and motivated Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist to join the Operations Support Bureau. This role supports fire investigation, hazmat operations, emergency management, and multi-agency coordination through the development and maintenance of geospatial tools, data systems, internal GIS web applications, and analytical products.

The GIS Specialist will design, maintain, and analyze spatial datasets; produce maps, dashboards, and reports; and serve as the HCFMO's primary geospatial resource in support of operational, investigative, and strategic decision-making. The position interfaces regularly with fire, EMS, and law enforcement agency partners across Harris County, and may support Emergency Operations Center (EOC) events.

The ideal candidate is technically proficient in ESRI products, comfortable with data integration and automation, able to support configuration-level maintenance of internal mapping applications (e.g., layer setup, symbology, access/permissions settings), and capable of translating complex geospatial information into clear, actionable products for command staff, public officials, and partner agencies.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Geospatial Analysis & Decision Support
Perform spatial analysis to support fire investigation, hazmat incident response, deployment planning, prevention, and risk reduction activities.
Develop and maintain data layers and geodatabases integrating internal records (incident, investigation, inspection) with external datasets (county parcels, Census, CAD feeds, utility infrastructure).
Analyze incident patterns, coverage gaps, response time performance, and risk density to support strategic and operational planning by command staff.
Produce recommendations and briefings derived from geospatial analysis for use by the Fire Marshal, division leadership, and partner agencies.
Evaluate data and access requirements for internal geospatial applications and recommend configuration changes to layers, symbology, or user permissions to better support analytical and operational needs.

Data Management & Quality Assurance
Design, build, and maintain geodatabases from multiple internal and external data sources in various formats.
Ensure spatial data accuracy, integrity, and consistency through systematic quality control and error-checking procedures.
Maintain geospatial data feeds required by Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) systems used by the HCFMO and regional dispatch partners.
Develop and document data standards, coding structures, and metadata to support business continuity and interoperability.
Apply change-control practices (e.g., testing and validating configuration or data changes before deployment to production systems) to minimize disruption to operational users.
Support maintenance of user and facility access permissions within internal geospatial applications, ensuring data governance and access-control settings remain accurate and current.

Cartography & Application Management
Produce and maintain print and digital maps for fire investigation, hazmat operations, fire prevention, special events, and administrative use.
Create and maintain ArcGIS Online web maps, dashboards, Survey123 forms, and mobile mapping applications used by field personnel.
Provide geospatial products and field support during large-scale incidents.
Maintain and update the mobile mapping environment for fire investigators and inspectors.
Configure and maintain layer settings, symbology, and feature-service connections within HCFMO's internal geospatial application(s), coordinating with technical/IT staff as needed for deeper platform-level changes.

Reporting & Data Visualization
Design and maintain operational and strategic reports and dashboards tailored to varied audiences, from field supervisors to elected officials.
Translate complex spatial data into clear visualizations (maps, charts, heat maps, infographics) that support retention and informed decision-making.
Integrate GIS products with other software platforms to support enterprise data workflows.

Coordination & Consultation
Serve as the HCFMO's GIS representative in regional geospatial working groups and inter-agency coordination bodies.
Collaborate with HCFMO divisions (investigations, hazmat, fire prevention, operations) and partner agencies to identify GIS needs and solutions.
Provide technical consultation and training to HCFMO personnel on GIS tools, data applications, and spatial query methods.
Support integration of GIS capabilities with UAS (drone) operations for incident mapping, post-fire documentation, and aerial data collection.

Automation & Workflow Development
Develop Python scripts, Model Builder workflows, and other automation tools to streamline routine data processing and reporting.
Evaluate and recommend new geospatial technologies, extensions, and integrations to improve HCFMO workflows.
Document all procedures, scripts, and automated workflows to ensure knowledge continuity.

Harris County is an Equal Opportunity Employer

https://hrrm.harriscountytx.gov/Pages/EqualEmploymentOpportunityPlan.aspx

If you need special services or accommodations, please call (713) 274-5445 or email ADACoordinator@bmd.hctx.net .

This position is subject to a criminal history check. Only relevant convictions will be considered and, even when considered, may not automatically disqualify the candidate.

Requirements

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems/Science, Geography, Computer Science, Emergency Management, or a closely related field

OR

An Associates degree plus
Three (3) years of directly relevant full-time experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree requirement

WITH

Minimum three (3) years of full-time experience in GIS analysis, data management, and cartography.
Demonstrated experience using ESRI ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and related extensions (Spatial Analyst, Network Analyst).
Experience creating and maintaining geodatabases and ensuring geospatial data quality and integrity.
Experience producing maps, dashboards, and analytical reports for operational or decision-making purposes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

GIS concepts, analytical techniques, and digital mapping principles.
ESRI product suite: ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online/Enterprise, and extensions.
Geodatabase design, maintenance, and spatial data quality assurance methods.
Statistical and analytical methods applicable to spatial data (clustering, network analysis, proximity, density).
CAD system geospatial data requirements and integration methods.
Emergency management frameworks including ICS/NIMS; EOC operations and GISS function.
GPS concepts and field data collection procedures.
Data governance and access-control principles as applied to enterprise GIS applications.
Perform complex spatial analysis to support tactical, operational, and strategic decision-making in a public safety environment.
Produce clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate maps, reports, and visualizations under time pressure.
Manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively in a dynamic, operational environment.
Explain technical geospatial concepts clearly to non-technical users, including command staff, investigators, and partner agency personnel.
Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining alignment with organizational priorities.
Establish effective working relationships with internal divisions and external partner agencies.
Respond and deploy for large-scale incidents, EOC activations, or other deployments as directed.

NOTICE:
Applicants for this position will be subject to a criminal background check that includes being fingerprinted. This applies to any position with network access to Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) or access to an area where CJIS is received, maintained, or stored either manually or electronically (i.e. custodian, maintenance).

Automatic Disqualification:

Convictions, probation, or deferred adjudication for any Felony, and any Class A Misdemeanor.
Convictions, probation, or deferred adjudication for a Class B Misdemeanor, if within the previous 10 years.
Open arrest for any criminal offense (Felony or Misdemeanor).
Family Violence conviction.

NOTE
:
Qualifying education, experience, knowledge, and skills must be documented on your job application. You may attach a resume to the application as supporting documentation but ONLY information stated on the application will be used for consideration. "See Resume"
will not be accepted for qualifications.

Preferences

Experience in a public safety, emergency management, or law enforcement environment.
ICS GISS (GIS Specialist) credential or eligibility to obtain.
GISP certification or Esri technical certification(s).
Proficiency with Python scripting or GIS Model Builder for workflow automation.
Experience with SQL, relational databases, Microsoft SQL Server, or Power BI.
Familiarity with UAV/UAS operations and integration of aerial imagery into GIS workflows.
Experience with AutoCAD, Survey123, QuickCapture, or similar field data collection platforms.
Familiarity with reading or editing basic JavaScript/TypeScript or JSON configuration.

General Information

Position Type and Typical Hours of Work:

Regular Full-time
Hours will be discussed during departmental interview.

Salary:

Minimum: $31.54 Hourly
Depends on Qualifications
Based on 26 Pay Periods
Plus, benefits

Work Environment:

Work is primarily performed in an office environment with regular use of computers and mapping systems.
The position may require field deployment to fire scenes, hazmat incidents, or EOC activations, including evenings and weekends.
Field work may involve exposure to outdoor conditions and environments associated with fire or hazmat incidents.
The GIS Specialist may be required to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds and must possess manual dexterity, clear speech, and visual/hearing acuity sufficient to perform the duties of the position.

Employment may be contingent on passing a drug screen and meeting other standards.

Due to a high volume of applications positions may close prior to the advertised closing date or at the discretion of the Hiring Department.

Map Data. Drive Decisions. Shape the Future.

Are you someone who sees the world in layers—of data, design, and discovery? Do you enjoy transforming information into robust planning, infrastructure, and public service tools? El Paso County is seeking a talented Geospatial Professional to join our Department of Public Works team and help build smarter, more connected communities through innovative GIS and asset management.

This is a career progression opportunity, with openings at the Associate, Analyst, and Senior Analyst levels.
Whether you're just starting your geospatial journey or are a seasoned GIS pro, there’s a place for you here to grow and make an impact.

As part of the Geospatial Analyst team, you’ll be key in maintaining and analyzing asset data for transportation systems, public infrastructure, and County resources. Your Work Has Meaning – Help plan and maintain the infrastructure that residents rely on every day.
Room to Grow – Our career progression path means your role grows as your skills do.
Use the Latest Tools – Get hands-on experience with cutting-edge GIS, programming, and asset management systems.
Collaborate Across Departments – Work closely with engineers, planners, field staff, and local agencies.
Be Part of a Mission-Driven Team – We’re passionate about service, innovation, and supporting each other.

Apply today to be part of a geospatial team where your skills and ideas truly make a difference!

jobs.title: Hydrologist I (MA/NH)
jobs.description:
Weston & Sampson is seeking an entry-level Hydrologist with 0-5 years of experience for our Water discipline in one of our MA or NH offices. The Hydrologist will have experience in hydrologic and hydraulic modeling, ideally with a focus on urban stormwater.

What you’ll do:

Conduct analyses and computer-aided evaluations of surface water systems, including watersheds, rivers, and lakes.

Model and support design of stormwater BMPs, green infrastructure, and LID projects.

Prepare Letter of Map Revision applications.

Become proficient with software such as HydroCAD, HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, and PCSWMM.

Work independently and effectively communicating results to a multidisciplinary team.

Prepare clear and concise written and verbal summaries of technical material for both technical and lay audiences.

Conduct field work to gather measurements, survey, and other observations to support surface water model development.

Some travel will be required to client meetings and project sites within New England and the mid-Atlantic and Carolinas.

What you’ll bring:

BS in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Hydrology, Hydrogeology, or similar degree is required.

MS in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Hydrology, Hydrogeology, or similar degree is a plus.

Engineer-in-Training (EIT) or ability to pass exam within the first six months of employment is preferred.

Experience with hydrologic (HydroCAD, HEC-HMS) and hydraulic modeling (HEC-RAS, SWMM) is preferred

Experience with GIS analyses and mapping is required.

Experience modeling and designing stormwater BMPs is a plus.

Experience modeling and designing green infrastructure and LID projects is a plus.

Successful candidates will have 0 to 5 years of experience and have a general familiarity with surface water hydrology and hydraulics.

Must have an interest in the evaluation and computer-aided modeling of surface water systems, including watersheds, rivers, and lakes.

Must be willing to collaborate remotely with coworkers in other office locations.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills and organizational/time management skills are required.

Must be willing/able to participate in field investigations. Some travel will be required to client meetings and project sites within New England. Valid driver’s license is required.

Salary Range $54,000 - $68,000 Based on Education

At Weston & Sampson, you’ll work alongside more than 1,000 employee-owners who are passionate about improving our communities. From providing clean water to designing resilient infrastructure and sustainable environments, our work has a direct impact on quality of life. We’re looking for curious, driven professionals who want to contribute to innovative, impactful projects and grow with a team that supports them.

We are a 100% employee-owned, interdisciplinary firm offering design, engineering, and environmental services. Since our founding in 1899, we have worked to build a collaborative, forward-thinking environment grounded in respect for each other’s ideas.

Ownership mindset: As an employee-owner, your work directly contributes to our shared success 

Growth opportunities: Build your career through mentorship, diverse projects, and clear advancement pathways

We believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. Weston & Sampson is committed to fostering a culture of belonging where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered. We actively support IDEA principles across our organization and in our daily work.

Ready to transform your environment? Let’s work together.

The Role – What You’ll Do

Barr is seeking a geologist to join our Minneapolis, Minnesota, office. In this hybrid role, you will support the Assessment and Remediation business unit and undertake challenging and progressive work on projects related to the investigation, evaluation, and remediation of contaminated sites. Assignments may include working as an individual or as part of a project team to assist with environmental site assessments; on-site investigations of contaminated soil, sediment, groundwater, surface water, and vapor; aquifer test performance and analysis; construction observation; development of site conceptual models; and preparation of drilling logs, geologic maps, cross-sections, and technical reports.

On-site investigation tasks may include observing drilling and monitoring well installation, classifying soil and bedrock samples, and collecting samples for field screening and laboratory analysis. Fieldwork opportunities for this position will be year-round and include some out-of-town travel.

The ideal candidate for this position is a clear and confident communicator who thrives in collaborative and independent work environments. They are adaptable, organized, proactive, eager to learn, and comfortable asking thoughtful questions. They bring a high level of attention to detail and take ownership of assigned tasks in dynamic field and office conditions. They demonstrate reliability, safety awareness, and a growth mindset as they build their technical skills and professional judgment. Above all, they value teamwork, quality, and integrity in delivering impactful environmental solutions.

Your Impact – Key Responsibilities

Technical knowledge: apply foundational geology/science principles to support site investigations, environmental sampling, and data collection. Assist in the analysis of environmental data and contribute to the development of remediation approaches.
Project support: help coordinate field activities and logistics, including contractor oversight and equipment preparation. Assist in tracking project progress and documenting key milestones.
Problem solving: contribute to the evaluation of site conditions and identification of potential solutions to environmental challenges. Learn how to apply regulatory knowledge and scientific reasoning to real-world scenarios.
Communication: produce clear field notes, chain-of-custodies, internal and external client emails, data summaries, figures, and draft report sections. Provide concise status updates to project managers and stakeholders.
Interpersonal savvy: effectively collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and clients to align technical work with project objectives while fostering strong, productive working relationships.

About The Opportunity

Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position is based out of Barr's Minneapolis, Minnesota, office.
Travel expectation: willingness to travel and periodically adjust personal schedule to meet project needs (up to 50% travel and 75% fieldwork expected; project needs will vary seasonally and over time).
Work environment: ability to work in locations that may feature rough terrain typical of construction sites and may also require entering and working in facilities that include limited accessibility, moving machinery, and other conditions typical of industrial facilities. Job assignments may involve work on waste disposal sites and sites requiring cleanup of hazardous materials. An OSHA-mandated physical exam may be required. Safety training will be provided. Applicants may be asked to participate in a drug screening program at the request of specific clients. Candidates must be able to perform job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Physical Requirements For The Role Will Include

Ability to conduct fieldwork in varying outdoor conditions (e.g., heat, cold, rain, uneven terrain).
Must be able to lift and carry equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
Must be able to work individually in remote locations.
Capable of standing, walking, kneeling, or crouching for extended periods.
Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required by site conditions.
Ability to safely operate or work around environmental monitoring and sampling equipment.

About You – Required Core Competencies

Education: bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, or geological engineering, or a related degree.
GPA: Minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0.
Software: Strong computer skills, including word processing and use of spreadsheets. Familiarity with Microsoft Office Suite.
Driver’s license: Possession of a current, valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.

Helpful Additional Experience (not Required)

Education: master’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, geological engineering, or a related degree.
Experience: 1–3 years of experience working on environmental sites.
Training: 40-hour Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response Standard (HAZWOPER) certification.
Licenses/certifications: fundamentals of Geology (FG) certified or ability to obtain certification within one year.
Familiarity with environmental regulations.

Compensation

jobs.title: Junior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
At SimPL Freight Solutions
, we simplify transportation for companies that move a lot of freight but don’t want the headache of managing it all themselves. We step in as their transportation team - coordinating shipments, managing carrier relationships, tracking performance, and improving how everything runs behind the scenes.

Our customers range from large manufacturers to high-volume distributors across industries like automotive, building materials, food, and packaging. No matter the industry, the goal is the same: keep freight moving smoothly, efficiently, and without surprises.

We pride ourselves on being proactive, responsive, and accountable - anticipating issues, communicating clearly, and continuously finding better ways to deliver results.

Position Overview

Are you naturally curious, comfortable working with numbers, and always asking why? SimPL Freight Solutions is looking for a Junior Data Analyst
who is excited to turn data into meaningful business insights.

This is an early-career opportunity designed for a recent graduate or someone beginning their analytics career. You will join a growing analytics department within a fast-growing logistics company, where your work will support real decisions involving clients, pricing, operations, and company strategy.

You will not be expected to know everything on day one. We are looking for someone with strong analytical foundations, attention to detail, and the drive to learn. You will receive guidance from experienced team members while gradually taking ownership of dashboards, reports, models, and improvement projects.

What You'll Do

Collect, clean, and validate client, prospect, pricing, and operational data
Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and visualizations using Excel, Power BI, Salesforce, and other tools
Analyze freight patterns, pricing, service performance, and business trends
Turn complex data into clear insights and recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences
Support pricing projects, client strategy reviews, sales presentations, and operational decisions
Partner with operations, sales, pricing, technology, and leadership on cross-functional projects
Identify data quality issues and help improve the accuracy and consistency of information across systems
Document and improve recurring reporting and analytical processes
Explore opportunities to automate workflows and use approved AI tools more effectively
Present findings and explain how they may affect clients or the business

What You'll Have The Opportunity To Learn

How analytics supports pricing, transportation, customer service, and business strategy
How to work with large, real-world datasets that may not always be perfectly organized
How to design dashboards and reports that business leaders actually use
How to translate a business question into a structured analysis
How to communicate findings to clients, managers, and company leadership
How to take an analytics project from an initial question through a final recommendation
How a growing analytics department develops its tools, processes, and standards

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Supply Chain Management, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field
0-2 years of relevant experience; internships, co-ops, academic projects, and related coursework are welcome
Coursework or project experience involving data cleaning, analysis, visualization, or reporting

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including formulas, lookups, pivot tables, and charts
Exposure to Power BI or another data visualization tool preferred; Salesforce experience is a plus
Exposure to SQL, data modeling, or database concepts through coursework or practical experience preferred
Strong attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving skills
Foundational data analysis and critical-thinking skills, with a willingness to learn
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Ability to explain findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Collaborative, dependable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities

We Offer

A competitive salary + bonus opportunities
Career growth, development, and advancement opportunities
Excellent benefits including:
Medical, Dental and Vision Insurances
Life and Disability Insurances
Company 401K plan with a company match
15 PTO days and 9 paid holidays

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

SimPL Freight Solutions is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive environment, welcoming and valuing our differences. Employment is based on individual merit and qualifications directly related to professional competence, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, sexual orientation, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. We value a diverse workforce that encompasses a wide range of perspectives, skills, and abilities.

Requirements And Preferences

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is seeking qualified candidates for the Program/Project Coordinator, Senior (E nvironmental Policy and Legislative Program Coordinator ) to support the Public Works & Environmental Services Department.

2026
Benefits of Broward County Employment

High Deductible Health Plan – Bi-weekly Premiums

Eleven (11) paid holidays each year

Up to 40 hours of Job Basis Leave for eligible positions

Tuition Reimbursement (Up to 2K annually)

The Position

This is an advanced professional position supporting the County’s environmental policy, resilience planning, and strategic energy initiatives. This position plays an important role serving as the lead environmental policy and legislative program coordinator for the Department. This position is responsible for the coordination and development of environmental policy recommendations, advocacy efforts, and implementation of related program initiatives in collaboration with internal, municipal and regional partners. The successful candidate will support county-wide and regional partnerships, including the County’s engagement in the 4-County Southeast Florida Regional Climate Change Compact. The successful candidate will also (1) perform high-profile management, communication, and research duties for County climate, resilience, energy, and water programs; (2) develop grant applications, oversee procurement, and manage diverse contract agreements with private sector, other governmental agencies, and non-profit partners; (3) support state and federal programmatic efforts and project partnership opportunities; (4) monitor evolving policy, legislation and regulations and develop advocacy plans; (5) participate, organize, convene, and staff various workgroups and committees; (6) serve as the Department’s policy expert on energy conservation and alternative energy initiatives. Work requires interagency collaborations, independent research, project ownership, stakeholder engagement, and accountability. Work is reviewed through regular meetings, reports and assignments.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Must have excellent communication skills, both orally and in writing, and strong presentation skills. Must demonstrate strong personal initiative; enjoy working as a team; and have superior organizational skills. The preferred candidate will be familiar with climate pressures within the South Florida landscape, and relevant climate mitigation and adaptation policy and programs at state and federal levels. Strong familiarity with the state and federal legislative process, and knowledge of diverse environmental subjects is preferred, including knowledge in the areas of energy, water resources, and Everglades restoration. Must have experience in building relationships with public, private, and academic partners. Must excel at completing projects within assigned timeframes while planning for future objectives. Demonstrated experience with graphics, website content management, communication tools, social media, and other on-line platforms is preferred

General Description

Administers large-scale programs and/or projects that have County-wide impact.

Works independently, under limited supervision, reporting major activities through periodic meetings.

Minimum Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major coursework in political science, public policy, environmental planning/science or closely related field.

(One year of relevant experience may be substituted for each year of required education.)

Requires four (4) years of experience in a staff or administrative capacity managing special projects, programs or business operations appropriate to the area of assignment or closely related experience.

Special Certifications and Licenses

Possess and maintain a valid Florida Class E Driver's License based on area of assignment.

Preferences

4+ years of experience in handling contracts/grant applications

4+ years of experience working with state/federal agencies.

4+ years of experience working with graphics, website/content management, communication tools, social media, and other online platforms.

SCOPE OF WORK

Duties And Responsibilities

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this class. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the job as necessary.

Plans, develops, authorizes, implements, supervises and evaluates programs/projects, activities and services on a large scale with County-wide impact; prepares reports, analyzes and interprets data.

Coordinates and manages all aspects of a program or project which has operational responsibility of a major scope, a large-sized budget and provides a critical County service.

Assists Director and Agency Leadership by researching issues, creating memorandums, policies, procedures, reports, etc. and monitors/advises on staff compliance with policy and procedures.

Conducts special research in conjunction with a project/program, analyzes data, and makes recommendations based upon research.

Identifies and understands agency/business needs, contractual business requirements, and regulations governing local, state and other requirements, confidentiality obligations, warranties, liabilities, indemnification, termination clauses, breach, and remedies.

Communicates business risks to project manager, senior/executive management, and approving authority for assessment and approval, while focusing on comprehending client-agencies' needs and business processes.

Coordinates with state and local agency partners on projects and programs, community outreach, media relations and regional and various services; may assist with press releases and responses to media.

Advises and assists the Department and Division Directors on all operational and technical matters related to the section(s) or function(s) assigned.

Defines agency goals and objectives, develops and recommends policies and operating procedures.

Administers internal/external communications and public outreach activities for Division; manages and coordinates outreach efforts with other County divisions as well as other local and state governments, and partnering agencies.

Prepares Commission agendas, including editing, posting and planning.

Provides assistance and training of agency staff and contracted services providers. May oversee the Agency's training program; schedules and/or delivers training and outreach opportunities for employees and the vendor community respectively.

Plans, organizes and implements a compliance and monitoring program, conducts contract central audits, field documentation reviews, investigations or management studies.

Plans, directs and supervises the activities of staff.

Performs related work as assigned.

Competencies

Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. Looks at complex issues from multiple angles; explores issues to uncover underlying issues and root causes; sees the main consequences and implications of different options.
Decision Quality: Makes good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward. Ensures that people's decisions comply with policies and standards. Integrates analysis, experience, and other inputs to make effective decisions. Accepts workable decisions and also seeks better alternatives.
Strategic Mindset: Seeing ahead to future possibilities and translating them into breakthrough strategies. Provides a clear picture of the organization's vision and strategy and what the team needs to do to realize them. Develops longer-term strategies that capitalize on the organization's distinct capabilities and emerging trends in the market.
Plans and Aligns: Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals. Stays focused on plans and improvises in response to changes, including risks and contingencies. Aligns own team's work with other workgroups'. Looks ahead to determine and obtain needed resources to complete plans.
Communicates Effectively: Develops and delivers multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Tailors communication content and style to the needs of others. Pays attention to others' input and perspectives, asks questions, and summarizes to confirm understanding.
Situational Adaptability: Adapts approach and demeanor in real time to match the shifting demands of different situations. Sees even subtle cues to adapt; deploys a wide range of behaviors to stay effective. Exemplifies flexibility and resourcefulness; responds deftly to a variety of challenges and situations.

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is seeking qualified candidates for the position of Natural Resources Specialist - regulatory-type field inspection concentration with the Pollution Prevention Section of the Environmental Permitting Division. The Pollution Prevention Section regulates, licenses, and inspects hazardous material, storage tank, and wellfield facilities in Broward County to protect the environment, ground and groundwater through applicable environmental regulations within the Broward County Code of Ordinances (the Code) and State and Federal Rules and Regulations.

Natural Resources Specialists with regulatory-type field inspection concentration conduct various routine regulatory compliance assistance and follow-up hazardous material and/or storage tank facility inspections; cite non-compliance items and issue non-compliance letters; prepare warnings and/or notices of violation and associated correspondence dealing with regulatory enforcement of environmental ordinances, rules and regulations; respond to haz-mat and/or storage tank associated Service Requests, citizen complaints, reported spills and discharges; and conduct field sweeps of industrial areas in search of regulated businesses operating without the required haz-mat/storage tank facility licenses. Storage tank facility type inspections also include install, closure, discharge investigation and complaint investigation inspections at State and County regulated facilities in Broward County. Regulatory-type field inspectors generally input their findings into the regulatory licensing and inspection databases, and maintain electronic files of documented observations, records reviewed, digital photos taken, test results received, site sketches, etc. and electronically issue associated inspection reports, notices and/or process other Regulated Enforcement activities to request regulatory-type Citation Warnings, Citations, Warning Notices and/or Notices of Violation to out-of-compliance regulated businesses in Broward County. Regulatory-type field inspectors must also possess and maintain strong technical and regulatory skills to coordinate and interact with Regulated Enforcement staff, Office of the County Attorney staff, and testify at Administrative Hearings while representing the County during Notices of Violation proceedings.

This hands-off position is mainly responsible for conducting regulatory-type field inspections at State and/or County regulated haz-mat and storage tank facilities in Broward County and ensuring compliance with all applicable environmental regulatory requirements. Tasks performed include educating the regulated community regarding the regulatory compliance program's purposes, requirements, processes and procedures; communicating with business representatives on-site in person, and/or by phone, email, or other written correspondence on regulatory compliance issues; scheduling regulatory inspections and associated follow-up activities; conducting electronic inspections by photo-documenting observations, inputting compliance and non-compliance findings, information into the databases; processing, maintaining and forwarding associated inspection reports electronically; citing non-compliance issues and processing and tracking associated enforcement activities to ultimately ensure regulatory compliance with licensing requirements and/or all applicable County, State and Federal Codes, Rules and Regulations.

Field Inspectors regularly coordinate internally with each other, Licensing Coordinator Natural Resources Specialists, Senior staff, Technical Support staff, Supervisors and/or Managers, and externally with Contractors, Permittees and/or the Regulated Community representatives regarding the Code and applicable inspections' rules, requirements, processes, procedures and regulations. Natural Resources Specialists in their capacity as regulatory-type field inspectors must possess strong customer service skills to coordinate, schedule and conduct regulatory field inspection activities, and the ability to communicate effectively and professionally in person, on the phone and in writing. Regulatory-type field inspectors must also possess knowledge of hazardous material facility and storage tank systems operations, strong organizational and computer skills, including the use of workflow databases, the Internet (for research and on-line business info, registration, etc.), MS Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, etc.) and Adobe Acrobat. Natural Resources Specialists are required to stay abreast of current applicable environmental technology and EPA, State and local rules and regulations and perform related work as assigned.

Uses digital/social media to benefit the team and add value to the work being done; understands how to avoid misuse of these tools.
Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. Quickly determines the most critical data and focuses analysis there; recognizes even subtle symptoms that indicate problems; probes deeply for root causes; uses systematic problem-solving methods. Well.

Optimizes Work Processes: Knows the most effective and efficient processes to get things done, with a focus on continuous improvement. Seeks out others' perspectives and asks good questions. Shares information that people want to know; gives appropriate context and details when speaking.

About The Company

Vanguard is a globally recognized investment management company committed to helping clients achieve their long-term financial goals. With a mission to put clients' interests first, Vanguard offers a wide range of investment products and services, including mutual funds, ETFs, and advisory solutions. The company prides itself on its client-centric approach, innovative strategies, and a culture of continuous learning and development. Vanguard's core values emphasize integrity, excellence, and a dedication to delivering value to its clients while fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment. As a leader in the financial industry, Vanguard continually invests in technology and talent to maintain its competitive edge and uphold its reputation for excellence.

About The Role

Vanguard is seeking an experienced Data Analyst to join its expanding Flagship & Distribution Analytics team. This role is pivotal in supporting the Flagship Client segment and the Distribution organization by analyzing complex data sets, identifying trends, and developing actionable insights that influence strategic decision-making. The ideal candidate will work closely with senior business leaders and cross-functional teams to design analytical solutions, influence outcomes, and proactively surface insights that drive business growth and operational efficiency. This position offers an exciting opportunity to leverage advanced analytics, machine learning, and data visualization techniques to shape the future of Vanguard's client engagement strategies.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will possess a minimum of 8 years of relevant analytics experience, demonstrating a strong technical background and a proven track record of influencing stakeholder decisions through data-driven insights. A bachelor's degree is required, with an advanced degree preferred, especially in fields such as Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or related disciplines. Candidates should have expertise in programming languages such as Python or R, and experience applying advanced analytical methods including predictive modeling and experimental design. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is the ability to translate complex data findings into clear, actionable recommendations. A demonstrated ability to lead projects, mentor team members, and foster a community of analytics excellence will be highly valued.

Responsibilities

Business Partnership & Problem Framing:
Engage with stakeholders to understand business strategies, define key questions, and structure ambiguous requests into clear analytical approaches. Lead complex, end-to-end projects that address enterprise-wide initiatives, serving as the analytics lead on cross-functional teams.

Data Management & Quality:
Acquire, synthesize, and manage structured and unstructured data from multiple sources. Ensure data quality, integrity, and consistency by establishing and maintaining high standards for data governance.

Advanced Analytics & Insight Generation:
Conduct complex analyses using advanced techniques, including machine learning, to uncover trends and generate insights. Validate methodologies to ensure analytical rigor and accuracy.

Storytelling & Executive Communication:
Develop compelling visualizations and insights tailored for executive audiences. Effectively communicate complex findings and translate them into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership.

Analytics Product Ownership:
Design, develop, and maintain recurring reports and analytics solutions. Promote best practices in data visualization and storytelling, mentoring team members to enhance their analytical communication skills.

Coaching & Community Building:
Mentor and coach analysts within the team, fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development. Contribute to the growth of the analytics community through knowledge sharing, training, and best practice development.

Additional Contributions:
Support special projects and broader team initiatives as needed, demonstrating flexibility and a proactive approach to organizational priorities.

Benefits

Vanguard offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and professional growth of its employees. This includes competitive compensation, health insurance plans, retirement savings options, and paid time off. Employees have access to ongoing learning and development programs, including training workshops, certifications, and mentorship opportunities. The company fosters a collaborative and inclusive culture, encouraging innovation and providing a flexible hybrid working environment that balances in-office collaboration with remote work. Vanguard also emphasizes work-life balance, employee wellness programs, and recognition initiatives to promote a positive and engaging workplace experience.

Equal Opportunity

Vanguard is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. Department:
